title: Hotpatch: adaptive-kernel misselection causing TTFT spikes on private & dedicated nodes
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: We observed customer escalations from multiple Private and Dedicated tenants (CUST-3342, CUST-3378) reporting large TTFT spikes and tokens/sec collapse during mixed-model fanout workloads. Root cause (current hypothesis): the adaptive kernel selection heuristic started mis-evaluating cost for small-batch long-context requests, preferring a quantized int8 kernel path that has higher per-token overhead on those code paths due to an unexpected cache-miss pattern and CPU/GPU affinity mismatch on Private nodes. This manifests as TTFT jumping from median ~350ms to >1.2s and sustained token throughput dropping from ~400 tps to ~80 tps for affected models. Impact: multiple customers on private clusters and a subset of Dedicated pools experienced degraded latency and throughput, triggering support escalations and revenue-impacting SLAs. Actions so far: 1) 2025-02-18 09:12 — Pager triggered; on-call engaged; created emergency incident channel and customer bridge. 2) 2025-02-18 10:00 — Reproduced issue in staging by replaying production traces (trace ids provided in links). Reproducer triggers when: (a) model fanout includes >1 large-context model and >2 small chat models concurrently; (b) context-length histogram skew >80th percentile; (c) workers with non-default CPU affinity. 3) 2025-02-18 12:30 — Temporary mitigation: pushed routing override to route affected tenants to fallback model-variant (float16 kernel) and disabled the adaptive int8 selection flag in the runtime config on Dedicated and Private control planes. This reduced TTFT on affected nodes to ~380ms and restored tokens/sec to ~360 tps within 15 minutes for the first cohort. 4) 2025-02-18 18:45 — Deployed a targeted hotpatch to kernel-selector heuristics (lowered int8 preference score when context >3k tokens or when batch-size <4) and introduced a short-circuit that falls back to float16 if prefix cache miss ratio >20%. 5) 2025-02-19 02:00 — Monitored 12h post-patch: rolling metrics look stable; two customers reported improvements and closed escalations. 6) 2025-02-19 14:00 — Added extra telemetry (kernel_choice, cache_miss_ratio, affinity_tag) with tagging for affected tenants. 7) 2025-02-20 09:00 — Began staged rollout of the updated heuristic to remaining Dedicated pools with canary percentage at 10% and automated rollback on SLO breach. Planned next steps: - Promote hotpatch into runtime-1.21 if canary holds; schedule non-urgent refactor to separate kernel scoring into a model-profile-driven table that avoids heuristics for known long-context models. - Add unit & integration tests that simulate mixed-model fanout and cache-miss patterns (check-in by eng:marcus/feature/kernel-selector-tests). - Postmortem and customer communication: collate timeline, RCA, and compensatory credit proposals; coordinate with CS for churn risk assessment. Acceptance criteria: stable median TTFT <= 450ms across affected tenants for 48h and tokens/sec within 10% of baseline under mixed fanout tests. Risks & open questions: - Are there other heuristics (batching, prefetch) that interact with kernel selector? early traces show batching windows being shortened unexpectedly under high-fanout. - Private nodes show higher variability due to custom CPU affinity configs; need a follow-up to ensure affinity-safe heuristics. - Security review: changes are config and heuristic only, but deployment in Private environments requires short review.
